# Working in this repository

This is the **public marketing and application-information site** for Elia,
served at <https://getelia.app> via GitHub Pages.

## The one thing that breaks work here

**Every `.html` file is generated by `tools/generate_i18n.py`** — including the
English pages at the root, and `sitemap.xml`. Editing HTML by hand looks like it
works and is then silently overwritten on the next generator run. This has
already cost one regression.

Change content in `tools/generate_i18n.py`, then run:

```bash
python3 tools/generate_i18n.py
```

`assets/css/styles.css` is the exception — it is hand-written and not generated.

## Scope boundaries

This repository is **not an Elia Platform client**. Do not design or implement
here: Elia Account login, family invitation flows, account management, Premium
management, synchronization, cloud data access, a family dashboard, or Supabase
integration. The site has no backend, no authenticated user area, and handles no
private family data. It has no current runtime dependency on Elia Platform.

- **Application implementation** belongs in the private application
  repositories. Pages here describe app behavior; they never define it. If the
  site and an app repository disagree, the app repository is right.
- **Account, family, Premium, synchronization, cloud, and security architecture**
  live in the private Elia Platform repository. Do not model platform concepts
  here — no data scopes, no sync entity lists, no backend architecture.
- **A platform-facing web client is not approved and not planned.** If a task
  seems to require one, stop and raise it rather than starting the work.

This repository is public. Do not put private repository URLs, SSH clone
addresses, workspace names, or other internal topology into it.

See [`docs/elia-ecosystem.md`](docs/elia-ecosystem.md) for the full boundary.

## Voice and medical boundary

Marketing copy is still Elia copy. The **private Elia Foundation repository** is
canonical for how Elia speaks and for what any Elia surface may say about health.
This site follows it; it does not set it.

The rules that bite hardest here, where enthusiasm is the occupational hazard:

- **No medical claims of any kind.** Never state or imply that an app assesses,
  monitors, detects, or reassures about health, labor progress, or a baby's
  wellbeing. No "normal", "healthy", "safe", "abnormal", or "warning" applied to a
  person. The apps record what a parent enters; the site must not promise more.
- **No pressure, no praise, no urgency.** No streaks, targets, countdowns,
  scarcity, "don't miss", or achievement framing.
- **Say less.** Calm, warm, plain. Never excited about someone's hardest hours.
- **Describe, do not evaluate.** The apps restate what a parent recorded; they do
  not analyse it. Copy implying insight, trends, or intelligence oversells the
  product and crosses the medical boundary at the same time.

A claim on this site that an app cannot honour is a defect, not marketing licence.
If a page needs to say something the boundary forbids, raise it rather than
softening the wording — the boundary changes in the Foundation, never here.

**The summary above is a public-safe approximation, deliberately.** The full rules
are private and are not reproduced here. That makes it a second copy that can go
stale: when the Foundation changes its voice or medical-boundary rules, this
section must be reviewed for drift and corrected in the same piece of work. Review
it by hand — there is no automated check, and none is planned for now.

## Conventions

- Internal links are root-relative and end in a slash (`/apps/feeding/`), never
  `index.html`. Canonical URLs, `hreflang`, and `sitemap.xml` must all agree.
- Three languages: English (root), German (`de/`), Spanish (`es/`). A copy change
  in one language means the same change in the other two.
- Privacy pages here mirror each app's own policy — update them together with
  the application repository, never independently.
- Do not invent repository URLs or product decisions. Record unknowns as
  explicit `TODO:` markers or open questions with complete question text.

## Verifying a change

Serve the site and check that pages and links resolve:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

## Project descriptor

`appmonto.yaml` at the repository root identifies this project and points at sources that already
exist here, for studio-level tooling. It carries data and references only — never commands,
credentials, checkout paths, status, version numbers, or copies of release evidence — and makes no
claim about release readiness or store availability.

Keep its `sources` paths correct when a referenced document moves. Do not add derived state to it:
if a fact already lives in a document, the descriptor points at that document instead.

## Where future work is recorded

- `docs/roadmap.md` is the only task source in this repository. Record intended work there, not
  in a new file, a handoff, or a comment — a second inventory drifts from the first and
  studio tooling will report it as an undeclared task source.
- One heading is one task. Bullets under it are its specification. If a bullet is
  something you would close and report on its own, give it its own heading.
- Each entry carries `**<ID>** · `<status>`` directly under its heading, where status is
  `ready`, `blocked` or `idea`. A `blocked` entry names its blocker on the same line. A
  `ready` entry carries a `**Done when:**` paragraph stating a checkable condition.
- Identifiers use the `EWEB-NNN` form and are never reused, including after deletion.
  Take the next number from the file's header and raise the header in the same change.
- Delete an entry once delivered, but only after the decision behind it is recorded
  outside the task file. Record the choice, its reason, and the constraint it places on
  future work — including decisions to stop or revert, which are the easiest to lose and
  save the most. "We did it" is not worth keeping; version control already has that.
- The exact grammar, including the markers for sections that are not tasks, is in the
  header of the task file itself.
